newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere shares seen up soon in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere shares seen up soon in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere B shares rose on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Tuesday amid considerable demand and brokers expected the company stock to pick up during the week.
"I'm positive on Solidere. I think it will be going up tomorrow. I wouldn't be surprised if the shares traded at $11 this week," a broker, who wished not to be identified, told Reuters.
B shares rose to $10.75 from $10.5 on Monday while Solidere A shares were unchanged at $10.5.

Heavy supply on A shares in recent days dragged the shares down. However, demand for A shares on Tuesday's first fixing was 176,788 against a supply of 122,458 while demand for B shares was 96,159 against a supply of 9,234.
The broker said some 450,000 Solidere shares were traded at prices ranging between $11 and $11.5 recently.
"People who bought at these prices will not sell for less then $11. They will wait until shares reach that level," he said.

Solidere shares slid last week after a surge stimulated by the rise in the company's Global Depositary Receipts in London and an expected announcement of 2.5 cents dividend at the annual shareholders' meeting scheduled for May 27.
However, brokers said last week the meeting would lack a quorum.
Of the three listed banks, Banque Libanaise pour Le Commerce fell to $16.25 from $16.5. The share fell to this level last week from $17.25 in profit-taking.
"BLC will consolidate at $16.25-$16.5 and will eventually pick up from there," the broker said.
Bank of Beirut fell back to Friday's level of $3.5625 from $3.625 on Monday while Banque Audi was unchanged at $20.
A block of 1,724 Audi shares traded on the floor at $20.
The LIBX bank index fell 1.08 percent to 136.71. The LISPI general index fell 0.54 percent to 86.08 while the BLOM general index rose 0.67 percent to 924.95.
"The market is now consolidating. We can see decent volumes and private investors buying," the broker said.
Of the four industrial companies listed, Ciments Libanais fell to $1.21875 from $1.28125 on turnover of 4,460 shares.

Total BSE turnover was 171,744 shares for a value of $1,476,947 from 345,151 shares for a value of $1,844,899 a day earlier. Monday's turnover included a block of 150,000 SCL shares traded at $1.28125 in the exchange.
There was no trade in either Ciments Blancs or Uniceramic.
